quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What is true about bicycles on the road?

options.text: They must always give the right-of-way to motor vehicles.
They do not have to follow traffic rules.
They are not a concern for drivers.
They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles. Drivers must respect bicyclists' rights on the road.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: On a two-way, two-lane road, you can pass safely only if:

options.text: You can see the road clearly ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle has enough power to pass.
All of the above are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above are true.
questions.explanation: Safe passing requires three things: you can see ahead clearly, you can return to your lane safely before oncoming traffic, and your vehicle has enough power to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard ciders or mixed drinks.
How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: On long trips, the best way to avoid drowsiness is to:

options.text: Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, take regular breaks to rest and stretch. Do this even if you do not feel tired yet.

questions.question: Orange signs warn you about:
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs with black letters warn drivers of work zones ahead. Workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: This sign indicates:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: If someone is injured in an accident, you should:

options.text: Move the injured person away immediately.
Not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. For heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop the flow.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Does not have to follow traffic laws.
Will always get just a warning.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ can cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road.
Take your hands off the wheel.
Take your attention away from driving.

questions.explanation: Distractions take your attention away from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel. Any of these can cause a crash.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: When you drive fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and your car slides on water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle will fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car might stall.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:
questions.explanation: When you see a flashing red light, you must stop and let all other traffic go first.

questions.question: Which of these can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: A downward-facing triangle sign tells drivers to:
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangle signs tell drivers to yield. You can go when the road is clear of traffic and pedestrians and it is safe.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane when you can see the front of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: This sign shape and color is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: Using drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol less harmful to your driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter) can impair your driving. Mixing drugs with alcohol greatly increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: ____ make it harder to stop and cause worse crashes.
questions.explanation: High speeds make it harder to stop and cause worse crashes. The faster you drive, the harder your car hits if there is a collision.

questions.question: When driving in rain, what lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain. They help you see better without reflecting back at you.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your body breaks it down more quickly.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reactions. It also makes you feel overconfident and causes you to make more mistakes while driving.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. Rescuers will find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. Rescuers will find you there.
questions.explanation: Stay in your car when stranded in a snowstorm. You are more likely to be found. Walking in a snowstorm is unsafe and may cause rescuers to miss you.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, not high beams. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even without flashing lights.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Traffic in both directions must stop. The bus may have an extended stop arm.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means that action is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and cars are backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is unsafe. Pull off the road and let cars pass. Only drive slowly when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What should you do if you experience a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not immediately use your brakes.
Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.

questions.explanation: If you have a blowout, release the gas pedal and avoid braking hard. Let the car slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the road.

questions.question: At a four-way stop sign, if two drivers arrive at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up their right-of-way.

questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to the driver on your right at a four-way stop if you arrive at the same time. You can then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. Always slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: A driver turning left at an intersection must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just like you would yield to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. Proceed only when the intersection is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Talking or texting on a cell phone while driving will not significantly increase your chances of being in a crash.
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving distracts you and increases your risk of a crash.

questions.question: You can drive above the posted speed limit to pass another vehicle on a road with a speed limit under 55 mph.
questions.explanation: On multilane roads where passing is allowed, you may pass on the left. Do not exceed the posted speed limit to complete a pass unless the speed limit is 55 mph or higher.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal to alert other drivers. Look for drivers also moving into the same lane. Never use your phone while driving to check road conditions.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.explanation: A white cane indicates the person is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. Protect this pedestrian from injury.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go onto the shoulder, reduce speed without hard braking. Carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic as you re-enter the road.

questions.question: Drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.explanation: Drive slower when the road is wet, slippery, or visibility is poor. Even if you drive within the speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May drive through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light allows you to drive through the intersection if it is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign prohibits it. Yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.
